anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: The After wording delivers the Change cleanly on this case: it accepts the numeric 2 as the one course selection, persists deliver with both 0/10 caps before writes, repairs P1 and CI-minted P2 with fresh helpers and closure review without any intermediate menu, renews the deadline only on the three own pushes (12:17, 12:25, 12:27) while explicitly marking the 12:11 BEHIND read as a base-only observation, auto-queues the sync, and renders a final that offers merge but executes nothing on stop. Checkpoints B and C now exit stuck on repeated red (B naming base-only SHA movement as not a source change, C with exactly one in-wave re-run and no second), and D persists pre_head B / expected_remote_head A, leases against A, and resets to clean B without a replayed push. Before failed every fact because it rejected the course vocabulary, refused to renew on own pushes, stopped at a BEHIND menu, and had no sync lease/restore model, so nothing Before kept was lost. One wording nit to watch in future cases: the main-sequence table says the round is 'counted at the source-changing commit' while the prose says usage was persisted before writes; keep both statements consistent (persist the checkpoint before dispatch, increment rounds_used only once a new repair-wave source commit exists) so the per-row accounting and the before-write persistence rule read as the same mechanism.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Before rejected the assess/deliver menu outright, so it never started the course, never pushed, never synced, never exited B/C on repeated red, and in D stopped before rebase — every fact failed there. After delivers all six: the initial `2` persists `course: deliver` and both caps/usage, P1 and CI-minted P2 are repaired in-course with no intermediate menu, the table records own-push deadlines 12:17/12:25/12:27 with the 12:11 base observation explicitly 'unchanged', BEHIND triggers the sync without a pick and final offers merge but the stop executes nothing, B and C both exit `stuck - red twice without a source change` (C after exactly one re-run), and D shows `pre_head: B` / `expected_remote_head: A`, a lease against A, and a clean restore to B with no second push. Nothing regressed; keep the compact head/usage/deadline/outcome table, the explicit base-observation-vs-push row, and the A/B lease-vs-recovery column — those are what make f2 and f6 verifiable. One minor tightening worth keeping: state in D that the sync counter increment is persisted alongside the restore heads, so the independent sync accounting is unambiguous under the new course model.
